items.title: S&P revises France's outlook from 'stable' to 'negative'
items.summary: Rating agency S&P revised France’s outlook to "negative" from "stable" on Friday, citing growing budget pressures as weak economic growth and higher interest costs make it harder to reduce the deficit.
items.t: S&P revises France's outlook from 'stable' to 'negative'

items.title: Uganda to withdraw troops from DR Congo
items.summary: First, Uganda is heading for the exit in eastern DR Congo. Kampala has announced the withdrawal of its troops from a key town in North Kivu, as relations with Kinshasa deteriorate following provocative comments from Uganda's army chief. Then, pregnant women are struggling to cope with extreme heat, while health experts warn of growing risks for unborn babies, from dehydration to premature births. And, after seeking safety, opportunity and a better life, many migrants in South Africa now face hostility, violence and growing exclusion. As anti-immigration sentiment gains ground, the country's promise is fading for those who once saw it as a land of hope.
items.t: Uganda to withdraw troops from DR Congo

items.title: ‘Abusive and insulting to Canadians’: campaign to oust US ambassador presented to parliament
items.summary:
Hundreds of thousands of Canadians call for Pete Hoekstra to be declared ‘persona non grata’

A petition signed by nearly 290,000 Canadians calling on Mark Carney’s government to oust Pete Hoekstra as US ambassador to Canada was formally presented to the House of Commons on Thursday, a sign of the strained relations between the neighboring countries.

Elizabeth May, a Canadian Green party member, originally opened the petition for signatures in July 2026 after a woman from Calgary sponsored it. The petition requests that the Canadian government declare Hoekstra “persona non grata” due to his “US” diplomatic interference in Canadian domestic affairs”.

Continue reading...
items.t: ‘Abusive and insulting to Canadians’: campaign to oust US ambassador presented to parliament

items.title: U.S. forces disable commercial ship that allegedly tried to breach Iran blockade
items.summary: A U.S. military aircraft struck a Palau-flagged ship with precision munitions after giving multiple warnings, U.S. Central Command said.
items.t: Trump says he's giving Iran "a chance to be smart"

items.title: Ukraine submits Black Sea ceasefire offer, awaits Russian response
items.summary: ⁠Ukraine ​made a Black Sea ceasefire offer ​to enable food exports and passed the details on to international allies, a senior Ukrainian official said Friday, adding that Kyiv was waiting for a response from Moscow. The announcement came a day after Russia attacked ​two foreign grain carriers near Ukraine's Black Sea port of Odesa, according to Ukrainian authorities.
items.t: Ukraine submits Black Sea ceasefire offer, awaits Russian response

items.title: 25-year sentence sought for former chef who aided 14 suicides
items.summary: Kenneth Law pleaded guilty earlier this year to aiding 14 suicides in Canada, but he has admitted to selling his so-called suicide kits globally.
items.t: 25-year sentence sought for former chef who aided 14 suicides

items.title: Spanish elections: 'Right-wing voters extremely mobilised, left-wing voters not mobilised enough'
items.summary: “His main political platform is to say, I am not Sánchez, I am the opposite of Sánchez.” As Spain heads to the polls, what do Alberto Núñez Feijóo's campaign and political career tell us about the kind of prime minister he might become? Javier Carbonell, Policy Analyst at the European Politics and Institutions Programme and lecturer at Sciences Po in Paris, joins Gavin Lee to break down the Popular Party leader's efforts to avoid the mistakes of 2023 and keep right-wing voters mobilised without galvanising the left.
items.t: Spanish elections: 'Right-wing voters extremely mobilised, left-wing voters not mobilised enough'

items.title: Canada: Supreme Court largely upholds Quebec secularism bill
items.summary: Quebec's government passed Bill 21 to ban religious symbols for public servants, arguing it was necessary to protect its secularist society. Critics argue the bill weakens legal protections for fundamental rights.
items.t: Canada: Supreme Court largely upholds Quebec secularism bill

items.title: The End of Spain’s ‘Frankenstein’ Coalition? Presidential Plotting in Paris, Kushner & Kremlin Trap
items.summary:
Catch up with the World This Week with Gavin Lee. In just 45 minutes, make sense of seven extraordinary days in global affairs, as Gavin and his handpicked panel of four leading international correspondents unpack the stories shaping the world — and the questions behind the headlines.

This week: Spain’s snap election; the presidential plotting unfolding over lunch at the Brasserie Concorde in Paris; Ukraine, Kushner and the ‘Kremlin Trap’; and the question hanging over Iran: whose side is time on?

Joining Gavin are New World Magazine columnist Emma-Kate Symonds; Constant Méheut, The New York Times correspondent in Ukraine; Venetia Rainer, Daily Telegraph Foreign Editor and host of Iran: The Latest; and Sarah Morris, France 24’s correspondent in Spain.
items.t: The End of Spain’s ‘Frankenstein’ Coalition? Presidential Plotting in Paris, Kushner & Kremlin Trap

items.title: U.S. opens hotline for tips about cartels, angering Mexico
items.summary: President Claudia Sheinbaum blasted the DEA after it set up anonymous tip lines in the country, accusing American officials of interference.
items.t: U.S. opens hotline for tips about cartels, angering Mexico

items.title: The AI revolution: Will I lose my job?
items.summary: Have you heard of FOBO? It stands for fear of being obsolete. So as AI spreads, is it going to impact women in the workforce more than men? And are we right to be fearful of becoming obsolete? The International Labour Organization has already found occupations dominated by women are nearly twice as likely to be exposed to job losses thanks to generative AI, compared to those dominated by men.
items.t: The AI revolution: Will I lose my job?

items.title: Police suspect criminals robbed fans at Manchester gig disrupted by ‘unknown substance’
items.summary:
Police are working with agencies across Europe after similar incidents occurred at two other Don Toliver concerts

A group of organised criminals are believed to have carried out robberies during Don Toliver’s Manchester concert, where an “unknown substance” was released, police have said, with similar incidents having occurred at another two of the US rapper’s gigs in Europe.

Greater Manchester police said they were working to identify the suspects and the substance involved during the incident at the Co-op Live Arena on Sunday evening.

Continue reading...
items.t: Police suspect criminals robbed fans at Manchester gig disrupted by ‘unknown substance’

items.title: Is Spain 'nostalgic' for Franco? Would traditional right PP consider an alliance with far-right Vox?
items.summary: After eight years of socialist-led government, Spain is at a crossroads. Can Pedro Sánchez pull off another electoral comeback, or will the conservative Partido Popular make way for the far right into national government for the first time since the end of Franco's 40-year brutal reign? Just back from Madrid, Richard Werly, Europe correspondent for the Swiss daily Blick, joins Angela Diffley to examine the final days of campaigning and the generational divisions shaping Sunday’s snap elections. The youth are divided between the left and the far-right Vox party. Sánchez, nicknamed the “Teflon politician”, has campaigned heavily on housing and social issues. “We may see an outgoing prime minister performing better than expected,” says Werly.
items.t: Is Spain 'nostalgic' for Franco? Would traditional right PP consider an alliance with far-right Vox?

items.title: 'From bad to catastrophic: Iran's justice system was already unfair for many decades'
items.summary: Amid war with the US and Israel, Iranian protesters continue to face death sentences following what Amnesty International describes as grossly unfair, torture-tainted trials. “The situation has changed from bad to catastrophic,” says Raha Bahreini, Iranian-Canadian human rights lawyer and Amnesty International's researcher on Iran. Bahreini discusses the aftermath of the January 2026 protests, the authorities' efforts to equate peaceful dissent with treason and espionage, and the extrajudicial killings of peaceful protesters. Amnesty International is calling for an international criminal justice mechanism, potentially a special tribunal. “There needs to be criminal accountability for these crimes against humanity.”
items.t: 'From bad to catastrophic: Iran's justice system was already unfair for many decades'

items.title: Uganda to withdraw troops from DR Congo town after army chief's threat sparks row
items.summary: Uganda's army on Friday said it planned to withdraw from the eastern DR Congo town of Lubero in North Kivu. The announcement came days after Ugandan army chief Muhoozi Kainerugaba – son of President Yoweri Museveni – threatened to take control of Walikale, another North Kivu town, sparking a diplomatic spat between the two neighbouring nations.
items.t: Uganda to withdraw troops from DR Congo town after army chief's threat sparks row

items.title: Spain races to stop oil spill after ship capsizes off Ibiza
items.summary: Spanish authorities raced to contain any damage to ecologically valuable Mediterranean waters on Thursday after a tanker carrying up to 7,000 tonnes of diesel capsized off Ibiza, leaving one dead.
items.t: Spain races to stop oil spill after ship capsizes off Ibiza

items.title: French far-left candidate Mélenchon demands ‘thorough overhaul’ of Germany ties
items.summary: Jean-Luc Mélenchon, leader of the hard-left France Unbowed (LFI) party, on Friday declared he was "hostile" to German economic liberalism and its dominance of the European Union. The septuagenarian presidential candidate in the 2027 race also warned that France could be drawn into unwanted conflict as Germany's growing military strength makes it a "target" for other countries.
items.t: French far-left candidate Mélenchon demands ‘thorough overhaul’ of Germany ties

items.title: Paris Paloma tackles Greek mythology, generative AI in her second album 'The Fatal Flaw'
items.summary: Dheepthika Laurent chats with Paris Paloma on set ahead of her Paris concert. The UK singer-songwriter and guitarist is promoting her second album, "The Fatal Flaw", an ode to Greek mythology, art and feminism. She tells us why this album is more personal than her first record, "Cacophony".
items.t: Paris Paloma tackles Greek mythology, generative AI in her second album 'The Fatal Flaw'

items.title: Google told to halt Belgium datacentre construction over lack of planning permit
items.summary:
Greenpeace publishes report showing tech firm is continuing to build despite planning appeal still unresolved

Belgian authorities have ordered Google to halt construction work on a large datacentre in the south of the country because the US tech firm’s requests to modify the original terms of the planning permission did not have approval.

“Inspectors visited the site and observed that the building was almost finished, with the structural work completed, even though the permit had been refused,” Raphaël Stokis, a Wallonia regional official, told the public broadcaster RTBF.

Continue reading...
items.t: Google told to halt Belgium datacentre construction over lack of planning permit

items.title: France is dealing with water insecurity – a new study shows it's a global problem
items.summary: Tens of thousands of people in France are living under water restrictions as the country deals with a drought despite recent rains, according to the environment ministry. But this is a global problem, as a new study released Wednesday revealed "the largest global decline in surface water resources recorded" since 1991, when data collection began.
items.t: France is dealing with water insecurity – a new study shows it's a global problem

items.title: Big EU defence projects under threat from proposed budget cuts: Commissioner Andrius Kubilius
items.summary: We speak to the EU's Commissioner for Defence and Space, Andrius Kubilius. The former prime minister of Lithuania – who grew up during the Soviet era – tells us how he sees the confrontation between Europe and Russia. He also sounds the alarm over proposed cuts in the EU's future budget, saying that they could jeopardise major European projects in defence and space. Kubilius praises the EU's SAFE defence loans programme, remarking that it has been "really very successful".
items.t: Big EU defence projects under threat from proposed budget cuts: Commissioner Andrius Kubilius

items.title: From cyberbullying to extremist content, can EU Kids Act protect minors online?
items.summary: Almost every European teenager is online. Some 96 percent of 15-year-olds use social media, yet many say they do not feel safe there. One in four children in the EU, aged 12 to 17, report having experienced cyberbullying, and nearly one in three say social media has left them feeling stressed, sad or socially excluded.
items.t: From cyberbullying to extremist content, can EU Kids Act protect minors online?

items.title: Divisions deepen between EU member states after tense budget summit
items.summary: An EU leaders summit on the bloc's seven-year budget fell apart amid divisions over how to fund Ukraine. The budget proposal also includes a 3% tax on US tech companies, in a bid for the EU to generate additional funds.
items.t: Divisions deepen between EU member states after tense budget summit

items.title: Jared Kushner’s 70-minute interview reveals naive bias in handling of Putin’s aggression
items.summary:
Trump’s son-in-law and senior negotiator paints Russian invasion of Ukraine as a misunderstanding to be resolved

In the space of a 70-minute interview, Jared Kushner – Donald Trump’s son-in-law and a prominent US negotiator in Russia, Gaza and Iran – probably did more to reveal why the world is mired in entrenched conflicts than a thousand geopolitical tomes or seminars.

During the conversation this week with Mathias Döpfner, the chief executive of the Axel Springer media publisher, Kushner gave a rare insight into his diplomatic technique, offering a string of homilies that veered close to banalities: “You have nothing until you have something”, “diplomacy is like untying knots on a fishing line for his son”, and “you play the ball from where it lands”.

Continue reading...
items.t: Jared Kushner’s 70-minute interview reveals perils of treating Putin like a corporate rival

items.title: Asia and Europe stocks rally after volatile week
items.summary: Stocks jumped on Wall Street on Friday, putting markets on track for strong weekly gains despite several days of erratic swings. Jameel Ahmad, Chief Analyst at GTC, tells us more.
items.t: Asia and Europe stocks rally after volatile week

items.title: Turkey summons Georgian envoy after football fans' pro-Palestine protest sparks clashes
items.summary: Turkey summoned ​Georgia's ambassador on ​Friday over violence that broke out ​at ‌a Europa ⁠League match in Batumi ‌between the Turkish Besiktas ⁠and Israeli Hapoel Beer-Sheva teams, according to a foreign ministry source. Clashes erupted after Besiktas fans unfurled a pro-Palestinian banner during the match, sparking the diplomatic row.
items.t: Turkey summons Georgian envoy after football fans' pro-Palestine protest sparks clashes

items.title: Sierra Leone: Maternal deaths fall as healthcare improves, but challenges remain
items.summary: Sierra Leone was once considered one of the most dangerous countries in the world to give birth. Maternal deaths have since fallen dramatically, thanks to improvements in healthcare, medical training and maternity services. But despite this progress, significant challenges remain. Activists warn that continued efforts are needed to ensure safer pregnancies and childbirth for women across the country. Clarisse Fortuné reports.
items.t: Sierra Leone: Maternal deaths fall as healthcare improves, but challenges remain

items.title: France: Macron lashes out at Le Pen’s ‘arrogance’
items.summary:
🇫🇷 French President Emmanuel #Macron on Thursday responded to far-right leader and 2027 presidential candidate Marine #LePen’s claim that he was “blocking” the French people’s freedom of expression.

Listen in to what he had to say.
items.t: France: Macron lashes out at Le Pen’s ‘arrogance’

items.title: DR Congo: Copper reserves put Africa at the centre of the global race for critical minerals
items.summary: Africa is emerging as a key player in the global race for copper, accounting for around 10 per cent of the world's estimated reserves. The Democratic Republic of Congo is at the centre of this growing interest, having mined 3.4 million metric tons of copper in 2025. Its vast mineral resources are attracting growing attention from countries and companies around the world, as demand for the metal rises due to its importance in energy infrastructure, electric vehicles and the global transition to cleaner energy.
items.t: DR Congo: Copper reserves put Africa at the centre of the global race for critical minerals

items.title: With Spain’s far right on the cusp of power, can women bail Sanchez out once again?
items.summary: Spanish women’s refusal to surrender hard-won rights helped Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez stave off defeat in a snap election three years ago. As he gambles with another early vote on Sunday, his hopes of defying the odds rest on women again rallying to block the far right from governing Spain for the first time since Franco’s dictatorship.
items.t: With Spain’s far right on the cusp of power, can women bail Sanchez out once again?

items.title: Nigeria: Political violence and attacks on candidates raise fears ahead of January elections
items.summary: Political violence is escalating in Nigeria ahead of the general elections scheduled for January. Candidates and their supporters have increasingly come under attack, with armed groups disrupting campaign rallies and some assaults resulting in deaths. Despite the growing number of incidents, security forces have struggled to contain the violence. With less than two months to go before the vote, fears are mounting that intimidation and deadly attacks could prevent many Nigerians from freely taking part in the democratic process.
items.t: Nigeria: Political violence and attacks on candidates raise fears ahead of January elections

items.title: Canada’s top court upholds Quebec law barring public sector workers from wearing religious symbols
items.summary:
Closely watched decision exposes tensions between minority rights and the power of government to override those rights

Canada’s top court has largely upheld a controversial secularism law in the province of Quebec barring public sector workers from wearing conspicuous religious symbols, in a closely watched decision that exposes the tensions between minority rights and the power of government to override those rights.

In a 6-1 ruling released on Friday morning, the supreme court found Quebec was permitted to shield the law, Bill 21, from most court challenges on the grounds that it violated charter rights.

Continue reading...
items.t: Canada’s top court upholds Quebec law barring public sector workers from wearing religious symbols

items.title: French student protests: A 'very bizarre' government response
items.summary: “The government had a very bizarre way of dealing with the student protests,” says Jean-Rémi Girard, a secondary school teacher and union representative in Asnières-sur-Seine. He explains how teachers sought to defuse tensions by listening to students, and respecting their right to protest, while keeping classes running. He recounts a police intervention last October and the case of a student facing trial for defending a classmate, and has the full support of several teachers. Girard questions the government's heavy-handed policing and largely symbolic proposals on class sizes and university admissions. “There wasn't really a negotiation,” he says, also highlighting the number of education workers injured during the protests.
items.t: Student movement in France: "The situation has varied greatly from one school to another"

items.title: Dutch authorities seize 26 critically endangered turtles from luggage of passenger bound for Hong Kong
items.summary: The tiny Vallarta mud turtle was only discovered in 2018. It's critically endangered with around 300 thought to live in the wild. Almost one tenth of that number were stashed in a traveler's luggage, bound in duct tape.
items.t: Dutch authorities seize 26 critically endangered turtles from luggage of passenger bound for Hong Kong

items.title: Norse Atlantic Airways files for bankruptcy and cancels all future flights
items.summary:
Norwegian airline tells customers not to come to airports after surging fuel costs caused by Iran war ruin finances

Norse Atlantic Airways has filed for bankruptcy and cancelled all future flights after surging fuel costs caused by the Iran war ruined its finances.

The Norwegian airline said it was entering insolvency and posted a message on its website telling customers not to come to airports – including passengers stranded away from home. Its collapse came a day after it put flights on hold with a warning that its finances were critical.

Continue reading...
items.t: Norse Atlantic Airways files for bankruptcy and cancels all future flights

Corrective Services NSW has been recommended to overhaul officer training for self-harm responses, and ban officers’ access to TV and YouTube while on shift.

items.title: Mad about mara: the DIY dance movement helping young Nigerians escape the daily grind
items.summary:
What started as one artist’s response to being cut out of a music video has exploded, becoming a driving force in Nigeria’s cultural landscape

As a student in the central Nigerian city of Ilorin, Lawal Habeeb Kola loved staying in his hostel room to produce beats rather than returning to his family house in Lagos, the more frenetic city of his birth.

In 2022, one of his beats became popular on TikTok, and a version featuring ad-libbed vocals from a hypeman sent it viral. He was invited to the music video shoot in Lagos and thought his big break had finally come, but when the video was released, he was absent.

items.title: New Zealand election: final results show ruling coalition needs minor party to govern
items.summary:
Incumbent prime minister Christopher Luxon loses majority and needs support of Opportunity party to remain in power, or country faces another election

The final results of New Zealand’s general election show the incumbent rightwing coalition will need the support of a centrist newcomer party to form a government, and to avoid sending the country back to the polls.

Preliminary results on 7 November handed the National party and its two coalition partners, the populist New Zealand First and libertarian Act parties, a slim two-seat majority, making the election too close to call until final votes were tallied.

items.title: Threat from China looms large over Taiwan’s local elections
items.summary:
Taiwanese officials raise alarm over interference by China in elections that will shape fortunes of ruling party

Taiwanese voters go to the polls on Saturday in closely watched local elections that will shape the fortunes of the ruling Democratic Progressive party (DPP) as it navigates an increasingly precarious set of relationships on the global stage.

Saturday’s vote will choose mayors, council members and other local leaders across 22 districts. Unlike the presidential elections, in which foreign policy is often a key issue, the local elections, held every four years, are largely focused on bread-and-butter issues such as housing affordability and wealth distribution.

Continue reading...
items.t: Threat from China looms large over Taiwan’s local elections

items.title: Albania's youth are protesting, no longer leaving the country
items.summary: Youth protests against a rigid political system and corruption have shaken the government of Albanian Prime Minister Edi Rama. They also show that fewer young people are willing to emigrate in search of a better future.

The US and Russia’s candidate for secretary general is on a charm offensive. Can she overcome London’s resistance to her bid?

Lana Nusseibeh is in Britain this week, attempting to present herself as a potential future UN secretary general, and shift the focus from her past as a United Arab Emirates diplomat who denied the country’s role in arming a militia accused of war crimes and genocide in Sudan’s four-year civil war.

items.title: China reserves right to take ‘necessary measures’ after Trump’s new tariff proposals
items.summary:
Beijing says new levies amount to ‘political manipulation’, while Brazil ‘will not yield to this type of threat’

  • Trump proposing new tariffs on 14 partners including China and EU

Beijing has said it reserves the right to take “necessary measures” after Donald Trump’s administration proposed new tariffs on goods from China and other major trading partners, triggering a global backlash.

Among the suggested levies on 14 major trading partners announced on Wednesday, China is potentially facing one of the biggest hits. It would face the highest capped rate of 20%, which in some cases will be stacked on top of other import taxes for a total rate of 45%.

items.title: ‘Trapped in grief’: wife of Japanese journalist detained by Russia pleads for his release
items.summary:
Yuki Imai being held in Moscow on allegations he conducted ‘espionage’ while working for a newspaper in Sakhalin island in Russia’s far east

The wife of a Japanese journalist who has been detained in Russia for more than a month on suspicion of spying has issued an emotive appeal for his release.

Yuki Imai, a reporter for the Hokkaido Shimbun, was arrested in mid-October as he was preparing to return to Japan from a two-year assignment at the Japanese newspaper’s bureau in the city of Yuzhno-Sakhalinsk, on the island of Sakhalin in Russia’s far east.

Blaze on ring road surrounding Egyptian capital injures at least 21 people and leaves cars and motorcycles charred

A crash involving a fuel tanker ignited a huge fire on a highway surrounding Cairo on Wednesday, killing at least 31 people, Egyptian authorities said.

The blaze on the ring road, a key artery that encircles the Egyptian capital, also injured at least 21 people and left more than two dozen cars and motorcycles charred, according to the latest figures released by the health ministry.

items.summary:
Unclear if ‘hostage-taker’ who was killed may have been a hostage as daylong siege in Cartagena shopping centre ends

Colombian police have stormed a supermarket in one of the country’s most popular tourist cities, ending a daylong siege in which all the hostages were freed and one man police described as a hostage-taker was killed.

Abelardo de la Espriella, the far-right president, travelled to the Caribbean port city of Cartagena to follow the final hours of negotiations and the tactical assault, in which special forces officers broke through blocked entrances and detonated stun grenades.

items.title: Lululemon founder stuns Canadian women’s leadership conference with sexist comments
items.summary:
Chip Wilson said men importing brides from Thailand was due to women waiting too long to have children

The controversial founder of Lululemon suggested women in Canada are having too few children and this could lead some men to bring in brides from Thailand, in remarks that stunned audience members at a women’s leadership conference.

Chip Wilson, who built the Vancouver yoga-wear startup into a global athleisure empire, was a featured speaker at the Leadership Forum in Calgary earlier this week, an event organized by Axis Connects to advance women in leadership. The organization says it aims to create space for “candid conversations about the barriers women face both in business and society”.

items.summary:
Muhammad Zeeshan Ali – the first Pakistani to reach orbit – greeted with Chinese ‘space handshake’ at Tiangong station

China has flown the first foreign astronaut to its Tiangong space station, starting what it says will be the globalisation of its space operations as the US-led International Space Station (ISS) enters its final years of operation.

Floating through a hatch to enter Tiangong, Pakistan’s Muhammad Zeeshan Ali grinned broadly as he was embraced by the onboard crew in what China’s space agency called the country’s first foreign “space handshake”.

items.title: Swiss tourist killed and British and Americans injured by elephants in Cameroon
items.summary:
Alain Throo, insurance executive based in London, reportedly gored and later died on hike near Mount Cameroon national park

A Swiss tourist has been killed and British and American tourists have been injured when a group of hikers encountered a herd of elephants in Cameroon.

The group of six tourists, four British, one Swiss and one American, accompanied by local guides, were hiking near the village of Bakingili in the south of the Mount Cameroon national park on 19 November, on a path used by elephants to access a nearby lake, when they encountered the herd of about 15 animals, according to media reports.

items.summary:
Kishanth Peramalya was denied entry due to sexual assault convictions and sent to Africa where he had no connections

The UK sent a Sri Lankan asylum seeker who had been convicted of sexual assault to Eswatini, a southern African country to which he had no connection and where he killed himself.

Kishanth Peramalya was part of a group that set sail from India hoping to reach Canada and claim asylum there. The boat was rescued by the Royal Navy in October 2021 when it got into difficulty and brought to Diego Garcia in the remote British Indian Ocean Territory, which hosts a US-UK military base.

items.title: Colombia’s president arrives at scene of supermarket hostage siege in tourist city
items.summary:
Abelardo de la Espriella to take control of operation trying to free at least 20 hostages

Colombia’s president has arrived at the scene of an hours-long standoff between security services and gunmen holding at least 20 people hostage inside a supermarket in Cartagena, a popular tourist city.

Abelardo de la Espriella’s motorcade arrived in Cartagena on Tuesday night, Agence France-Presse reported, where he will ostensibly take control of an operation involving scores of officers, the navy and special forces.
